title.heading:
The Dial:
a wireless knob
title.text:
Assemble it, flash it, bind it, turn it.
7 steps.

labels.title: Round display, 240 x 240
labels.text: It shows what the knob acts on. One button sits under the glass.

labels.title: Knob ring
labels.text: 16 detents a turn, a click for each.

labels.title: USB-C socket
labels.text: For flashing and for the console.

labels.title: Hand-held base
labels.text: Printed in two parts. One LiPo cell of 1,000 mAh lies in its lower part.

say.text: The M 5 stack dial is a wireless knob for the R C bench. This video shows how to put it into its printed base with a battery, flash it, bind it to the panel, and use it.
Its round display shows what the knob acts on. The ring around it turns in 16 detents, with a click for each. One button sits under the glass.
The U S B C socket at the back is for flashing and for the console.

labels.title: Top part
labels.text: Seats the Dial in a 45.2 mm hole. The opening at the side leads to the USB-C socket.

labels.title: Bottom part
labels.text: Holds the cell 102540, 1,000 mAh, in a pocket of 42.9 x 26.0 mm.

labels.title: The cell's plug
labels.text: Take the Stamp-S3 off: 2 screws M2. Plug the cell into the 2-pin socket under it, lead the wires out at the end away from the USB-C socket, put the Stamp-S3 back.

labels.title: Check the polarity first
labels.text: Match plus on the socket to plus on the cell's plug.

labels.title: Dial and ring nut
labels.text: The Dial through the top part, its USB-C socket in line with the opening. The ring nut goes on from below.

labels.title: Cell and foam pad
labels.text: The cell in its pocket, its wires on the side away from the USB opening. A foam pad of 2 mm, about 20 x 30 mm, on top: it holds the cell and leaves it room to swell.

labels.title: 4 screws M3 x 12
labels.text: Pan head, from the foot into the top part's bosses. Their heads sit 8 mm deep.

labels.title: Not printed yet
labels.text: No base has been printed, so no fit is tried.

say.text: Step 1. The dial goes into its hand-held base. The base is printed in two parts. The top part seats the dial. The bottom part holds one lithium polymer cell of 1000 milliamp hours.

First, the cell's plug. On the back of the dial, take off the stamp board, it is held by two small screws. Plug the cell into the socket under it. Lead the wires out at the end away from the U S B socket, and put the stamp board back. Check which pin is plus before you plug in.
Put the dial through the hole of the top part, with its U S B socket in line with the opening. Then turn the ring nut on from below.
Lay the cell into its pocket in the bottom part, with the wires on the side away from the U S B opening. A foam pad of 2 millimetres goes on top of it.
Close the base. Turn it over, and drive the four M 3 screws, 12 millimetres long, into the foot.
Turned back, the dial is ready to be flashed. No base has been printed yet, so this fit is not tried.

labels.title: Flash over USB
labels.text:
Connect the socket to a computer and write the merged image at offset 0x0:
python -m esptool --chip esp32s3 write-flash 0x0 rcbench-dial-merged-<version>.bin
A Dial that runs other firmware: hold the Stamp button while plugging in.

labels.title: NOT BOUND
labels.text: After the restart the Dial shows its name, DIAL- and 4 hex digits, and where to bind it.

say.text: Step 2. Flash the firmware over U S B. Connect the socket to a computer and write the merged image with E-S-P tool. A dial that runs other firmware needs its stamp button held while you plug it in.
After the restart, the dial shows, not bound, and its name.

steps.title: Switch the Dial on
steps.text: Set Dial to ON. The panel starts Bluetooth LE.
steps.say: Step 3. On the panel, open setup, wireless, dial. Set dial to on. The panel starts Bluetooth.

steps.title: Scan, tap, save
steps.text: Scan for Dial scans 10 s. A tap on Bound Dial lists what it found: tap yours, then SAVE.
points: One Dial is bound at a time
steps.say: Scan for dial scans for 10 seconds. A tap on bound dial lists the dials it found. Tap yours, then save. The scan is refused while the bench is armed.

steps.title: What a detent moves
steps.text: 1 % of throttle and 1° of horn angle by default. Each can be 0.5, 1, 2 or 5.
steps.say: Two rows set what a detent moves: 1 percent of throttle, and 1 degree of horn angle, by default.

labels.title: The turn moves the focus
labels.text: On the panel a ring marks the focused item; the Dial names it with its neighbours and its place. PRESS opens it.

labels.title: PRESS a value to set it
labels.text: The keypad opens and the turn moves the value by its step, inside its range. PRESS keeps it, HOLD cancels.

labels.title: HOLD goes back
labels.text: One level a hold. The Dial navigates only while the bench is SAFE, and no hold of the panel completes from it.

say.text: Step 4. The dial navigates the panel. Each detent moves the focus by one item. The panel marks it with a ring, the dial shows its name. A press opens it.
In a list, a press on a value opens it for setting. Now the turn changes the value, by its step, inside its range. A press keeps it. A hold cancels.
Outside a value, a hold goes back one level. All of this works only while the bench is safe.

labels.title: The same readings on both
labels.text: Six readings, a ring for each. While the bench is SAFE a turn moves nothing: ARM on the panel, with its 2 s hold.

labels.title: A detent is 1 % of throttle
labels.text: The panel and the Dial show the same run: throttle, speed, voltage, current and power.

labels.title: PRESS: throttle 0 %
labels.text: A press on the Dial's screen sets the throttle to 0 %. A HOLD of 1 s disarms.

say.text: Step 5. Open motor and E-S-C on the panel. The dial shows the same six readings, each with a ring. While the bench is safe, a turn moves nothing. Arm on the panel, with its 2 second hold.
Armed, each detent moves the throttle by 1 percent. The panel and the dial follow the same run.
A press on the dial's screen sets the throttle to zero. A hold of 1 second disarms.

labels.title: SERVO LIVE: a detent is 1°
labels.text: The horn on the panel and the commanded angle and pulse on the Dial move together.

labels.title: PRESS: CENTER
labels.text: A press centres the servo. A HOLD of 1 s disarms.

say.text: Step 6. On servo live, each detent moves the horn by 1 degree. The panel and the dial show the same angle and pulse.
A press centres the servo. A hold of 1 second disarms.

labels.title: Not a safety device
labels.text: STOP is on the panel only. ARM, SUPPLY ON, PROG 5V and WRITE stay the panel's 2 s holds: no turn or press switches power on.

labels.title: Link lost while ARMED
labels.text: 500 ms without a packet: LINK LOST, no turn is sent. After 1,000 ms the panel switches the bench SAFE, all outputs off.

labels.title: Forget the panel
labels.text: A 10 s hold of the screen button forgets the bound panel. Protocol version 1 has no pairing and no encryption.

say.text: Step 7. What the dial cannot do. It is not a safety device. Stop is on the panel only, and no turn or press ever switches power on.
If the link is lost while the bench is armed, the dial sends no more turns, and after 1 second the panel switches the bench to safe, with all outputs off.
A hold of 10 seconds forgets the bound panel. There is no pairing and no encryption yet.

scenes.heading: The Dial is bound and in use
items: Dial and cell into the printed base
scenes.say: The dial is bound and in use.
